subject: PHI ingestion exceptions and BAA applicability for patient uploads
messages:
From: Dr. Emily Ross <emily.ross@careatomics.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: security@careatomics.com <security@careatomics.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification: Are PHI 'ingestion exceptions' covered under Redwood BAA?

Hi Vivek,

Quick question from our engineering team as we prototype patient uploads: if a patient uploads a clinical PDF that contains PHI and we use Redwood's hosted endpoint for on-the-fly de-identification (we run an auto-redaction step client-side before sending, but edge cases exist where PHI may still be present in a single-page document), does Redwood consider that request "in scope" for a BAA?

A few details to help you answer:
- Upload flow: browser -> signed S3 URL -> Lambda preprocessor (client-side deid attempted) -> call to Redwood hosted /generate for text extraction and structured output
- We expect <1% of uploads to hit the hosted API with residual PHI due to OCR errors or free-text fields
- We need to know: 1) whether Redwood requires Dedicated/Private for any PHI in request payloads, 2) what logging/retention is applied to such requests, and 3) whether a DPIA or additional contractual language is required for these ingestion-exception cases.

Attaching a simple dataflow sketch (careatomics-dataflow-v1.pdf). Could you advise whether we should route those exception cases to Dedicated or if the hosted plan with a BAA amendment is sufficient?

Thanks,

Emily Ross, PhD
Head of Data Products
CareAtomics

[attachment: careatomics-dataflow-v1.pdf (diagram, 480KB)]

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference.com>
To: Dr. Emily Ross <emily.ross@careatomics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: Are PHI 'ingestion exceptions' covered under Redwood BAA?

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram. Tagging Laura (legal) and Karthik (security) to provide the formal guidance, but a few pragmatic notes from infra/product: 

- Short answer: any request with actual PHI in the request payload is treated as PHI-in-scope for contractual purposes. That typically pushes customers toward Dedicated or Private if they want strict isolation.
- Practical mitigation: for low-frequency ingestion exceptions we often recommend an automated routing rule: default hosted API for non-PHI, and a quick pre-check/heuristic that flags likely-PHI uploads and redirects those requests to Dedicated endpoints (our routing layer supports this).
- Logging & retention: hosted logs retain request metadata for 30 days by default; content-level retention can be configured per account (we can set policy to avoid storing payloads when the customer requests).

Can you confirm whether CareAtomics can: 1) keep the signed S3 object available to us for retrieval if we need to re-process, or 2) prefer that Redwood perform in-transit deid and then never persist original payloads? That will affect the BAA language.

I'll hand off to Laura & Karthik to call out contractual steps and evidence you'll need (SOC 2, DPIA notes, and a BAA amendment draft).

— Vivek
VP, Product — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
To: Dr. Emily Ross <emily.ross@careatomics.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Clarification: Are PHI 'ingestion exceptions' covered under Redwood BAA?

Emily — forwarding with the legal/security / evidence checklist. Please see inline below and attached a draft BAA snippet that covers ingestion exceptions.

>> Key legal points and asks:
>> - Scope: Any unredacted PHI in request payloads is in scope. If CareAtomics ensures client-side de-identification that removes PHI prior to transmission, those requests would generally be out of scope.
>> - Routing: If CareAtomics wants to keep using our hosted API for the majority of traffic but have a deterministic fallback for suspected-PHI, we can document a routing policy in the BAA and associated SLA.
>> - Evidence needed for procurement & compliance review:
>>   * Latest SOC 2 Type II report (we have this on file for Redwood; attached excerpt).
>>   * Dataflow diagram and sample retention configuration (we received your diagram).
>>   * DPIA or summary of processing risks for patient-identifiable data. If you don't have a DPIA yet, we can provide a short template.
>>   * Confirmation of encryption keys (KMS) usage and whether customer-managed keys are required.

>> Options for CareAtomics to expedite: 
>> 1) Dedicated-only approach: Redwood Dedicated + BAA admits all payload-level PHI; no additional redirection required.
>> 2) Hosted + routing policy: Hosted with BAA amendment and a deterministic routing rule that routes flagged payloads to a Dedicated pool; requires explicit routing policy in contract and minor logging adjustments (zero retention of raw payloads unless Customer permits).

I attached a short draft redline (redwood-draft-baa-snippet-20260830.docx) and an excerpt of our SOC2 (soc2-type2-2025-redwood.pdf). Review and let us know which path you prefer; we can then produce a formal amendment.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarification: Are PHI 'ingestion exceptions' covered under Redwood BAA?

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple quick items: 
- We will likely adopt the hosted + routing policy (option 2) to avoid the capex of Dedicated immediately. Can you confirm the maximum SLA for a routing decision (i.e., latency added by the routing check) and whether the redirect can be synchronous (return 307 to the client to hit Dedicated pool)?
- Security team asked for an example of the signed S3 URL pattern (we attach our current pattern) and the expected retention policy options you can configure per customer.

We'll review the draft BAA snippet and aim to return redlines next week. Can you also share the contact for Redwood's compliance lead to coordinate a short DPIA intake call?

Emily
